keyTerms.definition: N = 5.6e10, D/N = 5.4 at the data boundary.
Does loss keep falling past the cap with repeats?

recall.question: What breaks in the unconstrained argument?
recall.answer: The isoFLOP minimum is unreachable; the constrained optimum sits at the data boundary.

recall.question: List the three fixes in order of preference.
recall.answer: 1. Fewer KV heads (GQA-4): halves cache, no quality change expected. 2. KV quantization: small quality risk, needs eval. 3. Smaller batch: throughput cost.

recall.question: Which fixes change quality, and how do you check?
recall.answer: Fixes 1-2 touch quality. Check per-slice evals (U12-C10).

keyTerms.definition: Grow to n=200 plus a red-team probe set.

recall.question: Can you ship on the n=25 slice?
Design the cheapest valid safety gate.
recall.answer: Grow the slice to n=200 (half-width 0.038) plus a red-team probe set.

keyTerms.definition: 3.2 GB + overhead: feasible; the Bloom is unnecessary.

recall.question: Give Set 4's answers.
recall.answer: (a) 640 bits/item, k = 444. (b) FPR = 0.5^444 ≈ 0: effectively exact at this budget. (c) 1e8 hashes at ~32 bytes = 3.2 GB plus overhead: feasible, the Bloom is unnecessary here.

keyTerms.definition: Loss on assistant tokens incl. call JSON; 0 on tool results.

recall.question: Which tokens carry loss in the tool trace, and why?
recall.answer: Loss on assistant tokens incl. call JSON. 0 on tool results (observations, not behavior).

recall.question: The tool output contains user PII. What breaks, and the redesign?
recall.answer: The model reads PII it must not learn to emit; worse, the mask-0 text still sits in context. Redesign: redact tool outputs before training (U13-C07), never train on raw tool text.

keyTerms.definition: Advantages ~0 on 90% of groups: gradients vanish.

recall.question: What happens to the gradients with uniform groups?
recall.answer: Advantages ~0 on 90% of groups: gradients vanish, training stalls.

recall.question: Diagnose and fix.
recall.answer: Mean |advantage| near 0, reward variance near 0 per group. Fix: filter prompts to the learnable band (10%-90% success), resample the trivial ones out.

keyTerms.definition: Shed oldest first past the bound, version-aware.

recall.question: When does the queue fill, and what happens to staleness?
recall.answer: (a) Net +100/min: 10k/100 = 100 min. (b) Queue time grows; staleness KL blows past budget.

recall.question: Set the shed policy.
recall.answer: Shed oldest first past the bound, alert; the shed policy is version-aware (drop stale versions first).

keyTerms.definition: Fewer images, Perceiver compression, lower resolution.

recall.question: Does it fit, and what are the three ways?
recall.answer: (a) 12·256+2000 = 5072 > 4096: no. (b) 1. Fewer images. 2. Perceiver-style compression (needs training). 3. Lower resolution (quality cost on detail).

recall.question: Which preserves the most task performance, and how to test?
recall.answer: Test per-task accuracy vs image count on a held-out multimodal set; usually (1) wins when images are redundant.

keyTerms.definition: Slide content with page anchors; spoken content stays unknown.

recall.question: Update the source record for the surfaced G1 slides.
recall.answer: G1: slides inspected partial (pp. 1-40), recording missing.

recall.question: What can now be taught, and what stays unknown?
recall.answer: Slide content with page anchors, definitions and figures as shown. Spoken explanations, demos, Q&A stay unknown.

recall.question: Give Set 10's allocation and fleet size.
List the three gates before RL starts.
recall.answer: 1. SFT eval gate: instruction up, base not regressed. 2. Data manifest + lineage complete. 3. Safety probe suite passes.
